content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with a [product_name] master and slave module. I have programmed the master but it isn't recognizing the slave module. The master IP is set to 192.168.10.2, slave to 192.168.10.3, and PC to 192.168.10.4. The slave module has been configured to know the master’s IP. However, I keep encountering a network error code on the slave. Both devices are connected to an Ethernet switch through the PC. Can someone provide assistance? Thank you.

Hello, have you tried the following steps? 1. Connecting the master and slave directly with an Ethernet cable, without intermediary devices (no PC or switch). 2. Using a basic program on the master that only references a single input and output from the slave. 3. Pinging both device IP addresses from the PC to confirm network availability. Your setup description seems reasonable. If direct connection works but pinging from the PC fails, consider checking your switch. For example, some wireless routers with power saving modes might delay network responses until data starts transferring. Initially, you may not get a reply, but after a second attempt, communication is established. Hope this advice is useful.

Hello [user_name], You can refer to the following application example: [url] Scroll down in the link to find the relevant documentation detailing master-slave communication settings. Another possibility is that the IP address set in your program might not match what is configured on your [product_name] master device. To adjust the IP address in [product_name] software, go to the menu Tools -> Ethernet Connections. Next, in Tools -> Options -> Interface, verify that the IP address matches the master device configuration. Feel free to ask further questions.
Hello [user_name], When connecting two [product_name] modules via an Ethernet switch, you need to set both the subnet mask and gateway IP addresses. Hope this helps!

analysis.insight_summary: The central issue relates to configuring network communication between [product_name] master and slave modules over Ethernet. Users are experiencing persistent network errors on the slave unit, indicating that communication is not functioning correctly. Responses highlight the importance of properly matching IP addresses, subnet masks, gateways, and performing correct device and software setup. Access to clear documentation and intuitive software interfaces for network settings is crucial for effective troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate simple and clear configuration steps for connecting [product_name] devices, leading to seamless network communication once IP addresses are set. They also value feedback from both hardware and software to quickly diagnose and solve network problems.
